We implement appropriate security measures to protect your personal information against unauthorized access, alteration, disclosure, or destruction.

You have the right to access, update, or delete your personal information at any time. You may also opt out of receiving marketing communications from us.

We use cookies to enhance your experience on our website. You can choose to disable cookies through your browser settings, though this may affect the functionality of the site.

We may update this privacy policy from time to time. We will notify you of any changes by posting the new policy on this page.

8. Contact Us

If you have any questions about this Privacy Policy, please contact us.

The Extra Squeeze Grant

Uplifting Local Brands One Story at a Time

Apply Now

Watch: The Story Behind the Extra Squeeze Grant

A behind-the-scenes look at how Bogues Group and partners are using strategy, storytelling, and PR to give small businesses a bigger voice.

What Is the Extra Squeeze Grant?

The Extra Squeeze Grant is Springclean, CLT Five, Charlotte is Creative and Bogues Group’s way of giving back—offering grant funding, PR, branding, and creative support to local businesses making a difference. Whether it’s supplies, a media kit, video promo, or press strategy, we provide the extra squeeze to help brands shine. Each month winners are highlighted at Creative Mornings and CLT Five’s Instagram account!

Meet Our Recent Grant Partners

April's Main Squeeze

Phoenix Steele

Phoenix Steele, owner of Film Art, is a Charlotte-based makeup artist and a trusted creative force in fashion and film, known for blending bold artistry with inclusive impact. As an ally, she uses her talent to amplify diverse voices and create spaces where everyone feels seen, celebrated, and empowered.

May's Main Squeeze

Michelle Fernandez

Michelle Fernandez, owner of Fresh Squeeze, is a Charlotte-based creative committed to cultivating joy, connection, and mental well-being through art. As the founder of Fresh Squeeze, she leads inclusive, hands-on workshops that blend creativity with community care—making self-expression both accessible and restorative.

June's Main Squeeze

Grayson Sands

Grayson Sands, owner of Grayson’s Graphics, is a designer and creative force who brings bold ideas to life through chalk and other unique tools—crafting designs that speak, storytelling that sticks, and entertaining content that educates and inspires fellow graphic designers.

July's Main Squeeze

Shereese Floyd

Shereese Floyd, founder of Synthography Studios, is a Charlotte based visual AI artist who seeks to reflect humanity, celebrate black womanhood, honor creativity and ultimately move people with her artwork. Her portfolio doesn’t just showcase art—it sets a new standard for what’s possible with visual AI.

August's Main Squeeze

Linda Miller

Linda Miller, founder, Linda Miller Arts, is a self taught artist and shows that passion has no age limit. Establishing her business in 2022, her art work has been commissioned in Syracuse, NY between (1978 – 1990) and is scheduled to provide a 24 by 30 art submission for the January 2026 Cabarrus Art Guild event located at the Historic Courthouse in Concord, NC.

September's Main Squeeze

Tee Armstrong

Tee Armstrong is an author and entrepreneur, and the founder of Destined Butterflies, The Culture Shelf, Inner Mirror Collective, and her new venture, Destined For Your Business. A first-generation college student set to graduate in September 2025, Tee empowers youth through literacy, uplifts women in healing spaces, and fosters self-love, creativity, and resilience across diverse communities. Through Destined For Your Business, she provides administrative support, event planning, and business services while helping clients prioritize their time and self-care so they can grow and thrive. 

October's Main Squeeze

Jarrell Wallace

Jarrell Wallace, circus acrobat and community advocate, uses his artistry to empower and connect underserved communities. As a specialist in aerial straps and cyr wheel, he merges creativity with purpose—teaching capoeira alongside Instructor Reba Bowens at XLNC Dance Studio and leading circus arts classes for adults with developmental disabilities through Abound Health Day Support Center. Currently studying at Central Piedmont Community College, Jarrell is pursuing certification to work with at-risk youth and ultimately aims to earn his master’s in social work. Through the fusion of art and human services, he’s dedicated to helping others find strength, confidence, and connection.

November's Main Squeeze

Diana Spencer

Diana Spencer, Founder, The Art Princess, Christian mixed media artist who uses bold color and texture to reflect the beauty of spiritual transformation. Originally from Alabama and now in Charlotte, she creates vibrant, layered works and leads workshops—especially for children—that explore art as worship and self-expression. Her pieces have been featured in exhibitions and markets across the Carolinas.

December's Main Squeeze

Nada Esmaeel

Meet Nada Esmaeel, a multidisciplinary artist and illustrator based in Charlotte, North Carolina. Drawing from her ongoing reconnection to her Palestinian heritage, her work incorporates vibrant color and geometric motifs inspired by traditional tatreez embroidery, using mediums ranging from digital and ink to animation and textiles to celebrate cultural history, women, and the deep connection between land and people.

December's Main Squeeze

Corine Olarte VanderVoort

Meet Corine Olarte VanderVoort (she/they), a queer Filipina immigrant photographer based in Charlotte, NC, who creates transformative photo experiences rooted in radical self-acceptance and holistic empowerment. Through their Eat Like an Artist® community, podcast, and creative collective, Corine challenges the “starving artist” myth by fostering sustainable, supportive pathways for women and non-binary creatives to thrive.

March's Main Squeeze

Micah Harris

March’s Winner is CLT Youth Action Board/ Micah Harris, Micah Harris is the current Chairman of the CLT Youth Action Board (YAB), as the latest recipient of the Extra Squeeze Grant. Micah works alongside fellow members of the CLT Youth Action Board to develop initiatives that support and advocate for youth experiencing homelessness. Through his leadership and community collaboration, she continues to create opportunities for young people to be seen, heard, and supported.

Branding & Website Design

How BG can help build your brand? 

  • Logo

Branding and website design influences how visitors perceive and interact with your business online. A well-designed logo and website enhances user experience, strengthens brand identity, improves search engine visibility, and ultimately drives business growth and success.

  • First Impressions: Your website is often the first point of contact between your business and potential customers. A well-designed website creates a positive first impression, helping to establish trust and credibility with visitors.
  • User Experience (UX): Website design plays a crucial role in providing a smooth and intuitive user experience. A poorly designed website with confusing navigation, slow loading times, or cluttered layout can frustrate users and drive them away. On the other hand, a well-designed website enhances usability, making it easy for visitors to find the information they need and navigate through the site effortlessly.
  • Branding: Your website is an extension of your brand identity. Effective website design incorporates elements such as color schemes, typography, imagery, and logos that align with your brand’s personality and values. Consistent branding across your website helps to reinforce brand recognition and build brand loyalty among visitors.
  • SEO (Search Engine Optimization): Website design directly impacts your site’s visibility in search engine results. Search engines like Google consider factors such as mobile-friendliness, page speed, and structured data when ranking websites. A well-designed website that is optimized for SEO can improve your search engine rankings, making it easier for potential customers to find your business online.
  • Mobile Responsiveness: With an increasing number of people accessing the internet via mobile devices, it’s essential for your website to be mobile-responsive. Responsive design ensures that your website displays properly and functions seamlessly across various devices and screen sizes. A mobile-friendly website enhances user experience and helps to maximize engagement and conversions from mobile users.
  • Conversion Rate Optimization (CRO): Website design plays a crucial role in optimizing conversion rates. By strategically placing calls-to-action (CTAs), creating clear and compelling messaging, and streamlining the checkout process (for e-commerce sites), you can encourage visitors to take the desired actions, such as making a purchase, signing up for a newsletter, or filling out a contact form.
  • Competitive Advantage: In today’s digital landscape, having a well-designed website is essential for staying competitive. A professionally designed website sets you apart from competitors with outdated or poorly designed sites, positioning your business as a credible and trustworthy choice in the eyes of consumers.

 

Brand activation refers to the process of bringing a brand to life and engaging consumers through experiences that build emotional connections and drive brand loyalty.Bogues Group will work to create meaningful interactions and experiences that allow your consumers to experience your brand’s full values, personality, and offerings

How do we execute this? Through:

  • Creating Awareness and Build Equity: Brand activation initiatives aim to raise awareness about a brand, its products, or its services through events, promotions, or campaigns designed to attract attention and generate interest among target audiences.
  • Driving Engagement: Brand activation seeks to actively engage consumers and encourage participation through experiential marketing events, social media campaigns, or interactive content, the goal is to captivate audiences and foster meaningful interactions with the brand.
  • Creating Advocates: Effective brand activation can turn consumers into brand advocates who actively promote and endorse the brand to others. By delivering exceptional experiences and exceeding expectations, brands can cultivate a loyal base of customers who become ambassadors for the brand.

Don Anderson

​Don Anderson is Board Chair for GBCI, the organization that runs certification and credentialing around the LEED green buildings programs. He is an Operating Advisor to Blackstone, having served for ten years as Chief Sustainability Officer in its Portfolio Operations Group. Before joining Blackstone in 2011, Mr. Anderson was Vice President of Global Strategy and Business Development at ICF International, where he sold and managed energy efficiency and sustainability projects in the BRIC countries and Europe. Prior to that, he provided strategic consulting to portfolio-oriented corporations and programs associated with operational excellence and sustainability, including ENERGY STAR, USAID, USPS, DOE, and the U.S. Green Building Council (USGBC).

Michelle Diamandis

Michelle is a communications expert with 17+ years of experience working with brands across industries, with a special focus in CPG and alcoholic beverage brands. Michelle is the Co-Founder of TrueCraft Communications working with a variety of brands including cannabis, spirits and beer. Michelle loves working with clients to develop their stories and share them with the world.

David Eyl

Prior to joining Sportstoday, David Eyl was Vice President of Marketing for SFX Sports Group from 1998 through 2005. He holds a BA from Emory University, an MA in Sports Management from Ohio State University, and received a law degree from Temple University.

Sportstoday offers a cutting edge suite of online store, online ticketing and fan club services and solutions. A division of Live Nation Entertainment, Sportstoday is based in Charlottesville, VA. Clients include Tiger Woods, Dale Earnhardt Jr., Shaun White, Jeff Gordon, UVA Athletics, The Dave Matthews Band, USA Basketball, Jillian Michaels, and The AT&T Tiger Woods Foundation PGA Tour Event.

Rita Scott

Rita Scott is a pioneering broadcasting executive. She earned her B.A. in broadcasting with a business minor from Appalachian State University before launching her career in television sales. Scott held key positions at WGHP-TV, WJW-TV, ABC Inc., WBTV-TV, and WCSC-TV, where she became the first African American woman general manager of a local station in 1999. She served in this role until retiring in 2016. Throughout her career, Scott was active on numerous boards and was honored with Rita Littles Scott Day in Charleston and the Legacy Award in 2015. She currently resides in Charleston, South Carolina, with her two adult sons, Darren and Travis Littles.

Michelle Thomas

Michelle Thomas is a meticulous professional in the field of Corporate Social Responsibility, Government Relations, Innovation, Corporate Giving Programs, Brand Marketing, Public Relations, Grantmaking and Communications. Visionary leader, Keen knowledge in working with key stakeholders driving the rhythm-of-business process, strategic/investment planning & how it relates to shareholder value. Expertise in working with Government Elites both on the local, state and national levels, CEO’s, NGO’s, Business Leaders & Professional Athletes. Orchestration in the delivery of high profile/celebrity special events. Driven Award Winning Million Dollar Philanthropic Campaigns. High Achiever & Recognized as a key industry leader with demonstrated proven results.
